Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can put together a targeted gap analysis and an eval/regression plan. High-level notes below; I will attach a short two-page gap table and a proposed test plan by Friday.

Top-level positioning: Redwood considers the platform a serving/runtime and control plane that implements many technical measures for high-risk systems, but customers retain primary responsibility for training data provenance, labeling decisions, and high-level risk acceptance (per our Shared Responsibility Matrix). Where practical we provide turnkey tooling to help customers meet obligations (audit logs, versioning, model cards, human-in-the-loop hooks).

EU AI Act alignment (high level):
- Transparency & Information: model cards, per-request response metadata, and per-model provenance stored in the private control plane.
- Data governance & datasets: we provide hooks and metadata schemas but do not ingest customer training corpora on hosted tenants; for Dedicated/Private deployments, customers control dataset storage.
- Human oversight: configurable human-review checkpoints (sync/async) + function-calling to require approvals before generation in sensitive routes.
- Robustness & accuracy: continuous eval pipelines, regression alerts tied to test suites, and recommended quantization/precision profiles per model class.
- Record-keeping & logging: immutable request/response traces, token-level cost, and optional long-term audit retention (integrates with KMS/HSM).

We’ll deliver: 1) a gap analysis (red/yellow/green) with direct mappings to EU Act Articles and NIST AI RMF subcategories, 2) a proposed regression harness and scheduled evals (unit tests, safety prompts, edge-case fuzzing, and model-output drift metrics), and 3) a short matrix showing which obligations are platform-managed vs customer-managed.

Priyom will include a short technical appendix describing our regression harness and how we signal regressions. Laura — I’ll loop you on procurement language and a recommended contracting clause about audit access and data residency.

Karthik / Emily — quick technical clarifications and proposed eval approach (TL;DR below).

TL;DR: Our regression harness uses stable prompt suites + stratified input sampling from customer traffic (with opt-in sampling in hosted) and a dual-signal detection approach: functional regressions (task accuracy metrics) and distributional regressions (embedding drift + response token perplexity). We emit a regression event when both signals exceed tuned thresholds; owners receive an alert with failing prompts and diffed outputs.

Technical appendix (summary):
- Test corpus: canonical prompt sets (customer-provided) + Redwood-supplied scenario bank (safety, hallucination, PII redaction tests).
- Metrics: task-specific (BLEU/ROUGE/EM where applicable), token-level log-prob deltas, embedding cosine drift (baseline vs current), and safety classifier score shifts.
- Canary & rollout: every model update runs canary on a sampled production-like shard; failing canary -> automatic rollback and human review.
- Traceability: each eval record links to model version, kernel compile flags, quantization profile, and runtime hardware (for Dedicated).
- Human-in-the-loop: we surface low-confidence outputs to a reviewer queue with built-in accept/reject signals to retrain or flag prompts.

Open questions for Emily: do you need supporting language on retention windows for logs (we support configurable retention; enterprise default is 1 year with add-on for longer), and any specific thresholds SCAHealth uses for drift alerts?

Attaching a draft gap analysis table and the proposed regression plan as promised.

Regards,
Priyom
